# Project Overview

BibVik is a pipeline for analyzing citational practices in Viking Age archaeology.
Starting from a seed paper (Lund & Sindbæk 2022, "Crossing the Maelstrom"),
it extracts the bibliographies of 382 papers that cite it (F1 generation),
builds a citation graph, and produces structured data for network analysis
and citational practice research.

The corpus spans multiple languages (Norwegian, Swedish, Danish, German, French,
English) and diverse publication types — journal articles, edited volumes,
monographs, grey literature — with non-Latin characters throughout. Standard
scholarly metadata databases (Scopus, WoS, OpenAlex) have poor coverage of
this material, which is why references are extracted directly from PDFs.

The project is connected to the workshop *Citational Politics and Practices
in Viking Age Archaeology and Beyond*, organized with Julie Lund and Isak
Roalkvam at the University of Oslo.

More at [zackbatist.info/BibVik/](https://zackbatist.info/BibVik/).

# Technical Environment

- Python 3.12+, running on a GPU cluster (`buckeridge-rtx6000`, GPUs 5–9,
  Quadro RTX 6000) with a NAS at `~/models/`
- GROBID 0.8.1 via Docker on `localhost:8070`
- Ollama with `qwen3:35b` (thinking mode disabled via `"think": false`)
- F1 PDFs at `~/models/BibVik_seed/`
- Outputs at `~/models/BibVik_output/`
- Codebase at `~/models/BibVik/CitationAnalysis/`
- Zotero CSV (`BibVik_seed.csv`) for PDF↔citekey matching — read-only,
  do not modify

# Module Map

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `detector.py` | Multi-method citation detection (6 methods applied per paper) |
| `resolver.py` | Resolves unmatched citations via LLM inference from contexts |
| `graph.py` | Builds multi-generational citation graph with deduplication |
| `tei_parser.py` | Parses GROBID's TEI-XML; extracts body, footnotes, references div |
| `grobid_client.py` | HTTP client for GROBID; OCR fallbacks (ocrmypdf, pdftoppm+Tesseract) |
| `normalize.py` | Per-entry normalisation applied at graph construction time |
| `enricher.py` | CrossRef enrichment — additive metadata, never identification |
| `postprocess.py` | LLM cleaning passes run after enrichment; applies corrections.yaml |
| `corrections.py` | Manual bibliography curation via corrections.yaml |
| `audit.py` | Diagnostic HTML report assessing bibliography quality |
| `exporter.py` | Graph export to GraphML, GEXF, and CSV formats |
| `coverage.py` | PDF coverage reporting and OA acquisition via Unpaywall |
| `context_extractor.py` | Extracts verbatim citation contexts *(tabled)* |
| `metadata.py` | Controlled vocabularies and output metadata |
| `zotero_csv.py` | Zotero CSV import for exact PDF↔citekey matching |
| `biblatex_model.py` | Biblatex data model and completeness scoring |
| `utils.py` | Config, citekey generation, I/O, signal handling |

# Citation Detection: Six Methods

For each paper in the corpus, six detection methods are applied independently.
Their results are merged and deduplicated into a single set of citations. Each
citation is tagged with which methods found it (provenance tracking).

## Method 1: GROBID Bibliography

GROBID's ML models parse the PDF's reference list into structured `<biblStruct>`
entries. This yields the richest metadata (title, journal, volume, pages, DOI)
when it works.

**Strengths**: Rich structured metadata. DOIs when available.

**Weaknesses**: Trained on STEM articles. Misses footnote-style references.
Fails on non-standard layouts. Splits entries across PDF page breaks.

## Method 2: GROBID Inline Markers

GROBID annotates `<ref type="bibr">` elements in the body text. (Author, year)
pairs are extracted from the marker text independently of whether the
corresponding bibliography entry was successfully parsed.

**Strengths**: ML-detected, handles diverse inline styles.

**Weaknesses**: Only catches citations GROBID recognised as references.

## Method 3: Regex Patterns

Pattern matching for standard citation forms in the raw body text: parenthetical
`(Smith 2020)`, narrative `Smith (2020)`, multi-author, et al., semicolon-
separated groups. Handles non-English connectors (og, und, och, et).

**Strengths**: Fast. Catches formally styled citations GROBID missed.

**Weaknesses**: Cannot detect discursive references or organisational authors.
Unreliable for multilingual text.

## Method 4: LLM Body Scan

Each paragraph is sent to the local LLM with a prompt asking it to identify all
referenced works. This catches discursive references, organisational authors,
and any citation style recognisable to the LLM.

**Strengths**: Most comprehensive detection. Handles any citation style.

**Weaknesses**: Slowest method. May produce false positives.

## Method 5: LLM Footnote Extraction

Each footnote containing year patterns is sent to the LLM with a structured
extraction prompt. The LLM returns full bibliographic metadata — not just
(author, year) but title, journal, volume, pages, entry type. Essential for
papers using Chicago footnote style.

**Strengths**: Extracts rich metadata from footnote prose. Handles multiple
references per footnote.

**Weaknesses**: Depends on LLM accuracy.

## Method 6: LLM Bibliography Re-parse

The raw text of the `<div type="references">` element in the TEI back section
is sent to the LLM in a single call. This text is continuous across PDF page
breaks — unlike GROBID's parsed `<biblStruct>` entries. Method 6 recovers
entries that GROBID's structured parser missed due to page-break fragmentation,
dash-abbreviated author series, and title extraction failures.

**Strengths**: Recovers entries invisible to all other methods. Handles any
bibliography format.

**Weaknesses**: Depends on the references div being populated (20 of 382 papers
have empty reference divs due to chapter-style formatting).

## Merging

After all six methods run, results are merged by normalised (author, year) key.
When multiple methods detect the same citation, their provenance tags are
combined.

# OCR Fallback

`grobid_client.py` implements two OCR fallback paths:

**ocrmypdf** (standard): when GROBID returns `[NO_BLOCKS]` for a scanned PDF,
`ocrmypdf` adds a text layer, the original is backed up to `output/ocr/originals/`,
and GROBID retries.

**pdftoppm + Tesseract** (alternate): when GROBID returns `[BAD_INPUT_DATA]`
(structural PDF failure) or the extracted text has high private-use Unicode
density (font encoding failure), the PDF is rendered to page images at 300 DPI
and OCR'd with Tesseract (nor+swe+dan+deu+eng+fra+pol+ukr). The resulting PDF
is cached in `output/ocr/` and resubmitted to GROBID. If the fallback still
produces degraded output, entries from that paper are flagged `_ocr_candidate`
and surfaced as draft delete corrections.

# Resolution

For citations detected in the text but not matched to any existing bibliography
entry, the resolver uses only the LLM. CrossRef is not used for resolution —
author+year queries to CrossRef produce a high rate of false positives because
CrossRef always returns a result regardless of domain. See
`docs/methods/resolver.md` for the full rationale.

The LLM receives up to three citation contexts and infers full bibliographic
metadata. If no contexts are available, the entry becomes a stub preserving the
citation relationship without metadata.

# Graph Construction

The citation graph is built incrementally:

1. **Seed paper**: Extract all citations (6 methods). Add to bibliography as F1.
2. **F1 papers**: For each PDF, extract all citations (6 methods). Match the
   paper to its existing F1 entry. Add its citations as F2.
3. **Deduplication**: Each new entry is checked against existing entries by four
   strategies in order: DOI, exact title, author+year+fuzzy title, and
   cross-script transliteration (Cyrillic ↔ Latin via ALA-LC / `domovyk`).
4. **Per-paper enrichment**: Each newly added entry is enriched via CrossRef
   immediately after insertion, so its title is available for deduplication of
   subsequent papers.

Matching an F1 PDF to its bibliography entry uses a tiered strategy: Zotero CSV
→ DOI → exact title → author+year.

# Normalisation

Normalisation runs per-entry at creation time inside `normalize_entry()` in
`normalize.py`. Every new entry is normalised before being added to the bibliography.
See `docs/methods/deduplication-normalisation.md`.

# Enrichment

After the full corpus is processed, `--enrich` fills in missing metadata fields
from CrossRef. Two strategies: DOI lookup (fully reliable) and title query
(accepted only at ≥0.85 title similarity). Enrichment is strictly additive —
existing fields are never overwritten. See `docs/methods/resolver.md`.

# Post-processing

`--postprocess` runs as follows:

1. **Pass 0: Corrections** — applies `corrections.yaml` (merge, delete, set, split)
2. **Pass 1: Entry type reclassification** — uses enriched fields to correct
   types, with guards against false reclassification
3. **Pass 2: Author recovery** — LLM extracts authors from raw citation strings
   for NOAUTHOR entries; failures become draft set candidates
4. **Pass 3: Title recovery** — LLM extracts titles from raw citation strings
   for entries missing one
5. **Draft corrections** — pipeline flags appended to `corrections.yaml` as
   `_draft: true` for researcher review

Near-duplicate resolution as a standalone LLM pass (`flag_near_duplicates()`
in `postprocess.py`) exists in the codebase but is not currently wired into
the `--postprocess` pipeline — deduplication is handled at creation time
during graph construction instead (see `docs/methods/deduplication-normalisation.md`).

# Corrections

`corrections.yaml` in the project root is the single file for all manual
bibliography curation. Four action types: merge, delete, set, split. Notes
required on all confirmed entries. Pipeline-generated drafts (`_draft: true`)
are appended after each `--postprocess` run. See `docs/methods/corrections-system.md`.

# Completeness Scoring

Each bibliography entry receives a `completeness` field with a score (0.0–1.0)
and a breakdown of which fields are present vs. expected for its entry type.

# Audit

`--audit` produces a diagnostic HTML report (`output/audit_report.html`)
assessing bibliography quality across five dimensions: completeness, accuracy,
representational consistency, coverage, and provenance. Read-only — corrective
actions go in `corrections.yaml`. See `docs/methods/audit-sampling.md`.

# Export

`--export` produces four output files via `exporter.py`. Tombstoned entries
are excluded as nodes, with one exception: an entry deleted (not merged) that
appears as a citer elsewhere is retained as a flagged "ghost" node so its
outbound citation edges are not lost on export. Entries tombstoned via merge
are fully excluded, since their outbound relationships were already remapped
onto the surviving entry during the merge itself.

- `citation_graph.graphml` — for R/igraph
- `citation_graph.gexf` — for Gephi
- `citation_edgelist.csv` — directed source→target pairs
- `citation_nodes.csv` — node attributes: title, year, generation, entry_type,
  first_author, doi, completeness, in/out degree

# Graceful Cancellation

Ctrl-C during a long-running stage writes the current bibliography state to
`_partial_bibliography.json` before exiting.

# CLI Flags

| Flag | Stage | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | 1-4 | Run full pipeline |
| `--extract` | 1 | Seed paper only |
| `--iterate-f1` | 2 | F1 papers → citation graph |
| `--enrich` | 3 | CrossRef enrichment of bibliography |
| `--enrich-bib-only` | 3 | Bibliography enrichment only |
| `--enrich-auth-only` | 3 | Author enrichment only |
| `--postprocess` | 4 | Apply corrections, LLM cleaning passes, generate draft corrections |
| `--audit` | 5 | Diagnostic HTML quality report |
| `--export` | 6 | Export graph to GraphML, GEXF, CSV |
| `--coverage` | — | PDF coverage report + OA lookup via Unpaywall |
| `--audit-n N` | — | Sample size per audit section (default: 10) |
| `--audit-seed N` | — | Random seed for audit sampling (default: 42) |
| `--audit-threshold F` | — | Duplicate similarity threshold (default: 0.70) |
| `--limit N` | 2 | Process only N F1 papers |
| `--email` | 2,3 | Contact email for CrossRef polite pool and Unpaywall |
| `--model` | 2,4 | Override LLM model name |
| `--remote` | 2,4 | Use remote cluster LLM (reads llm.remote_url from config) |
| `--no-think` | 2,4 | Append /no_think to LLM prompts (Qwen3 only) |
| `--verbose` | all | Debug logging |
